plan.summary: This 1-4 block is an off-camp boxing build focused on general strength, simple explosive work, and enough conditioning to support skill training without dragging recovery. Week 1 establishes training maxes for the main percentage-based lifts, one lift per session, and the main training work starts in Week 2. Weeks 2-3 build steady volume with crisp intent, and Week 4 deloads by cutting volume while keeping the main patterns in place.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Establish baselines, build squat-press-pull strength, and keep power and aerobic work simple and repeatable.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Increase force output on the main lifts and keep explosive work sharp with manageable fatigue.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Shift more of the work toward faster power and sharper boxing-relevant output while maintaining strength.

exercises.name: 1a. Box Jump
exercises.notes: Use a low box and stick the landing. Every rep should look fast and clean.

substitutionOptions.name: Countermovement Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if boxes are awkward or crowded. Jump for height and land softly.

exercises.name: 1b. Medicine Ball Rotational Scoop Throw
exercises.notes: Throw hard from the hips, reset between reps, and use a non-bouncing or low-bouncing ball.

substitutionOptions.name: Medicine Ball Shotput Throw
substitutionOptions.notes: Good option if wall space is limited. Drive from the rear hip and finish tall.

exercises.name: 2. Back Squat
exercises.notes: Warm up gradually, then work up to one hard top set of 3-5 reps with solid depth and control. This establishes your baseline for future percentage work.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then work up to your heaviest clean set of 3-5 reps. Stop with good form and log the load and reps so the app can set future percentages.

substitutionOptions.name: Front Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the back squat rack position is uncomfortable. Keep the torso tall and stop if form folds.

exercises.name: 3a. Chest-Supported Row
exercises.notes: Drive the elbows back and pause briefly at the top. Keep the chest planted.

substitutionOptions.name: Seated Cable Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a neutral or medium grip and keep the torso still.

exercises.name: 3b. Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.notes: Brace hard and only roll as far as you can without the low back sagging.

substitutionOptions.name: Barbell Rollout
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if no ab wheel is available. Keep the same braced position.

exercises.name: 4. Farmer Carry
exercises.notes: Walk tall with tight ribs and quiet steps. Use a load you can control without leaning.

exercises.name: 1a. Medicine Ball Chest Pass
exercises.notes: Throw each rep hard with a quick reset. Use a moderate-bouncing or non-bouncing ball.

substitutionOptions.name: Plyo Push-Up to Box
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a box or bench to keep impact low. Aim for fast hands and clean landing.

exercises.name: 1b. Band-Resisted Pogo Jumps
exercises.notes: Stay stiff through the ankles and keep contacts quick and light.

substitutionOptions.name: Line Pogos
substitutionOptions.notes: Simple low-impact option if no bands are set up.

exercises.name: 2. Bench Press
exercises.notes: Warm up gradually, then work up to one hard top set of 3-5 reps with a stable touch point and smooth lockout. This establishes your baseline for future percentage work.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then work up to your heaviest clean set of 3-5 reps. Keep your form tight and log the load and reps so the app can set future percentages.

substitutionOptions.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if barbells are limited. Keep both bells moving evenly.

exercises.name: 3a. One-Arm Dumbbell Row
exercises.notes: Pull toward the hip and keep the torso quiet. Do not twist to finish the rep.

substitutionOptions.name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Good swap if you want more torso support.

exercises.name: 3b. Half-Kneeling Cable Lift
exercises.notes: Move through the trunk and shoulders without leaning back. Stay tall through the front hip.

exercises.name: 4. Neck Flexion and Extension Isometric
exercises.notes: Use gentle resistance and keep the neck long. This should feel controlled, not grindy.

exercises.name: 1a. Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Jump fast, land soft, and reset between reps. Stop if height drops off.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Good option if you want a simpler jump with no dip timing.

exercises.name: 1b. Medicine Ball Overhead Slam
exercises.notes: Drive the ball hard and reset every rep. Use a non-bouncing ball.

substitutionOptions.name: Medicine Ball Scoop Slam
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the slam area is tight.

exercises.name: 2. Romanian Deadlift
exercises.notes: Warm up gradually, then work up to one hard top set of 4-5 reps. Keep the bar close, hinge cleanly, and stop before your back position changes. This establishes your baseline for future percentage work.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then work up to your heaviest clean set of 4-5 reps. Log the load and reps so the app can set future percentages.

substitutionOptions.name: Barbell Hip Thrust
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if hinging is uncomfortable. Drive through full hip extension without over-arching.

exercises.name: 3a. Rear-Foot Elevated Split Squat
exercises.notes: Stay balanced and let the front leg do the work. Keep the torso slightly forward.

substitutionOptions.name: Dumbbell Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Simpler option if balance is the limiting factor.

exercises.name: 3b. Lat Pulldown
exercises.notes: Use a controlled pull and full reach at the top. Stop each set with 1-2 reps in reserve.

substitutionOptions.name: Assisted Pull-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you want a more vertical pull with bodyweight involvement.

exercises.name: 4. Assault Bike Aerobic Intervals
exercises.notes: Keep the pace steady and repeatable. You should finish feeling worked but not wrecked.

endurancePrescription.target: Build aerobic support without extra impact

substitutionOptions.name: Lateral Bound to Stick
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you have more space and good landing control.

exercises.name: 1b. Medicine Ball Rotational Punch Throw
exercises.notes: Move fast through the hips and shoulders and fully reset each rep. Use a low-bouncing or non-bouncing ball.

substitutionOptions.name: Medicine Ball Side Throw
substitutionOptions.notes: Simple wall-based option with the same rotational emphasis.

exercises.name: 2. Front-Foot Elevated Split Squat
exercises.notes: Warm up gradually, then work up to one hard top set of 4 reps per side. Keep the front foot flat and stay controlled through the bottom. This establishes your baseline for future percentage work.

substitutionOptions.name: Dumbbell Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if setting up the front-foot elevation is inconvenient.

exercises.name: 3a. Standing Dumbbell Overhead Press
exercises.notes: Brace hard and press in a straight line. Do not lean back to finish the rep.

substitutionOptions.name: Half-Kneeling Landmine Press
substitutionOptions.notes: Safer option if overhead pressing feels awkward.

exercises.name: 3b. Cable Crunch
exercises.notes: Round through the trunk and keep the hips still. Make the abs do the work.

exercises.name: 4. Heavy Bag Tempo Rounds
exercises.notes: Stay technical and smooth. This is conditioning through steady work, not a brawl.
